answer: Every AI agent must enter through a remote-attestation inlet that binds its identity to a manufacturer-fused key inside one secure enclave CPU. The registry then plants that key in an orchard of admitted roots and assigns a weekly proof-of-inference puzzle seeded by the key plus a randomness beacon, sized to consume the whole core. In the reputation grove, any duplicate key or skipped puzzle prunes the identity. An attacker creating sybils must rent one enclave-equipped machine per fake agent and burn a full core continuously for each, so cost scales linearly with identities.
